chapter: After Cab: Don Redman, teaching and records
title: Ending the studio; publishing; BMI deal; losing his Joe Davis rights
summary: The studio lasts two years, a publishing firm folds, and Thomas explains how he lost royalties on his Joe Davis records.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yeah, he was a great player. So how long, did you and Cozy have a studio?

We had it about two years. But Cozy kept going in and out of town. And we had a publishing company, but Cozy never did...he never did contribute to the publishing company, so it just went kerplunk. I had a good deal, too. And I wrote his book, but I didn't give him a chance to write my books. I had a deal with BMI. It was a terrific deal, too, because they would publish anything, and when they got the money back from the publisher, I got 35 percent and they took 25 percent. And that's when I should

have done all my writing. But I was busy teaching, and my recording, my other recordings... I got (?) on a lot of records with Joe Davis, because I sold them again to somebody else. But he can't do nothin' about it, because I called him to merchandise my records under another name, under Coleman Hawkins' name...
What was Joe Davis' (?). He didn't have no rights to them, huh?

No. I had rights. But I lost them... Somehow or another, with all the moving I did, I lost my contract. Because my contract read that if they were ever produced in any other way, then I had royalties on them. But see, he paid me outright, and I guess I didn't look carefully at it... I was making so much money, getting the money, a hundred dollars, a hundred and fifty dollars and so on...
That seemed to have happened with a lot of us, especially Black performers.
Yeah. See, I was making the money for the arrangements...
That's the same thing that Jelly Roll did...
Right. I got the money for the arrangements. But I got paid for my tunes. But I only got paid for that
one specific date as long as he had them on the Joe Davis label. But I was told...
